subject: Minute-window buffer and retrograde credit agreement
messages:
From: Elena Martin <elena@clearshore.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, ops@fastlane.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected minute-window spike during launch — request for buffer/credit

Hi Ben,

Quick note from this morning's launch: we saw several short-lived but very high-concurrency bursts — roughly 14 minutes of elevated QPS in the 03:00-03:20 UTC window — that pushed us well past our agreed minute-level throttle. The attached usage_report_June.csv shows the pattern.

We planned the launch around our committed throughput but the burst pattern was more spiky than expected (client-side fanout on a new feature). We got throttled hard and that caused retries and retry-thundering which magnified the token volume.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood temporarily lift the minute-window throttle for ClearShore for a short window (we're asking +20% headroom for 72 hours) so we can stabilize without repeated throttles?
- Can you provide a retroactive credit or smoothing on the overages from that 03:00-03:20 UTC period? We expect this will be a one-off; we'd like to avoid full-list price overage for an operational spike tied to our rollout.

We can provide a PO immediately if needed. Ops is cc'd (ops@fastlane.ai) — they manage our infra.

Thanks for quick help,
Elena

--
Elena Martin
Head of Product, ClearShore
elena@clearshore.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachment: usage_report_June.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martin <elena@clearshore.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected minute-window spike during launch — request for buffer/credit

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear reproduction and the CSV. I pulled the same window and can see the short, high-amplitude spikes. Two things we can do immediately to keep your rollout healthy and to make the billing outcome fair:

1) Temporary minute-window buffer (operational)
   - We can enable a +20% minute-headroom on your minute concurrency limit for a 72-hour window starting when you confirm. This will be a soft limit: we'll still throttle above it but the higher internal floor should reduce retry cascades.

2) Retrograde credit (billing) — our proposal
   - For any overrun that occurred during the identified 03:00-03:20 UTC window, Redwood will apply a retroactive credit equal to 40% of the incremental overage cost above your committed threshold for that window. The remaining 60% will be invoiced at your standard overage rate.
   - Credit mechanics: the credit will be applied across your next two monthly invoices (50% on the next invoice, 50% on the following). We won't change the token bucket or base rates; this is a one-off customer good-faith remediation tied to the launch spike.

Operational next steps: confirm the start time for the 72-hour buffer and we'll flip the switch. Billing/legal next steps: Laura and Karthik — can you confirm finance/legal are OK with the 40% retrograde credit and the 2-invoice application? I can prepare a short amendment to the MSA (one page) for Elena to sign; I attached a draft (proposed_amendment_HL-4829.docx).

If that's acceptable to ClearShore we'll also add a small invoice note describing the credit so their accounting team can reconcile.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0123

Attachments: proposed_amendment_HL-4829.docx (DOCX, 12KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Unexpected minute-window spike during launch — credit proposal (HL-4829)

Laura / Karthik — forwarding ClearShore's request and my proposal. Quick financial impact calc below so we can move fast:

- Observed incremental overage (03:00-03:20 UTC window): ~1.2M tokens above commit (extracted from usage_report_June.csv).
- Incremental overage cost at published rate: $360 (example: $0.0003/token) — (use final rates from finance).
- Proposed credit (40%): $144 credit applied to next two invoices ($72, $72).

This is intentionally modest; it preserves unit economics while giving the customer a meaningful remediation and avoids escalation. The temporary +20% minute buffer should prevent additional throttling and (we hope) further overage.

Questions:
- Legal: any wording concerns with the proposed amendment? I kept it narrow and time-bound (72-hour buffer + one-off credit).
- Finance: confirm the billing flow — can you record a negative line item and amortize it across the next two invoices? Or should we treat it as a one-time credit in the next invoice?

If you sign off I'll route the doc to Elena via DocuSign and schedule the buffer start once they confirm PO.

Thanks — Ben

From: Elena Martin <elena@clearshore.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fastlane.ai
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected minute-window spike during launch — request for buffer/credit

Ben — thank you, this is exactly what we were hoping for. ClearShore accepts the +20% minute buffer for 72 hours and the 40% retrograde credit split across the next two invoices.

Next steps on our side:
- We'll send PO HL-4829-PO1 by EOD tomorrow (ops@fastlane.ai will attach).
- Please route the amendment via DocuSign to elena@clearshore.com (we need it signed before the buffer goes live).
- Please add the following invoice note on the next invoice: "Launch spike credit (HL-4829) — 40% credit applied to 2027-06-14 03:00–03:20 UTC window." That'll help reconciliation.

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the pragmatic approach.

Best,
Elena
